answers.ask: What should the course itself look like - bright candy platforms, a neon speed-run aesthetic, or something else? Only the characters were described as anime.
answers.answer: Use a bright, colorful anime-inspired speed-run aesthetic with clean floating platforms and obvious parkour obstacles.

answers.ask: Roughly how many levels should ship in the first build?
answers.answer: Ship 5 course levels for the first build, each requiring more speed and awarding more wins than the last.

scene_prompt: Create a bright, colorful anime-inspired speed-run parkour map with clean floating platforms and obvious obstacles. Arrange five distinct course levels in increasing difficulty, each as a separate elevated route with longer or more demanding parkour sections than the previous level; provide a clear starting area and progression toward the higher-level courses.
agent_notes: This is the "+1 speed" family: the number going up is the game, speed is bought with upgrades and wins buy better characters, so it is Simulation with preset Stat Grinder, and the parkour course is named second rather than allowed to lead. The shape is tier-ladder - five course levels of rising speed requirement, each walled off until the stat crosses the threshold, which is exactly the tiers-in-a-line-with-a-gate-between-them layout, and it keeps the build on P0. I took obstacle-jump from Obby & Platformer for the bright floating-platform parkour the answers describe, but deliberately not path-track, because its P6 would validate physics-legal gaps this game does not need - here the barrier is the speed number, not the geometry. Without a user I kept the preset's rebirth pad at the far end of the last tier even though no rebirth was named, since buying better anime characters is the permanent-multiplier step the family always ends on, and read social-hub as the character shop wins are spent at.
